reviews.Text: Been using this for years, but just found out a third-party testing lab found Redmond Real Seat Salt to be high in lead. As it turns out, it is apparently very hard to keep heavy metals out of salt that is mined from the ground. Go to the Lead Safe Mama website and look up their salt testing results. As a result of their findings I have decided to just use Kirkland (Costco) brand Sea Salt, which did not get into the best category, but was satisfactory, and much less lead than Redmond, as well as much more affordable.

reviews.Text: Bought this Redmond Sea Salt based on reviews and claims by the manufacturer. Finally left a teaspoon of the salt in a glass of water overnight and was disturbed to see much sediment on the bottom of the glass, a brownish-red color. Poured it onto a paper towel, and tasted it. It was not salty, but tasted like rock or dirt. Have attached a photo. Then was equally disturbed to read that Lead Safe Mama and Mamavation tested it and results showed Lead between 250 and 290 ppb. It's in the trash now. Money wasted.

reviews.Author: SweetSweet
reviews.OriginDescription: Reviewed in the United States on November 20, 2025
reviews.Text: Add another dislike to the list for all the crunchy sand that's in this salt. This salt is mined, so they capture a lot of stone matrix along with the salt, and since it's unrefined, that ground up stone makes it into the final product. If you put this on your food, you will crunch on sand particles with your teeth. It's very unpleasant. Imagine going to a restaurant and having your food have crunchy sand on it. You would send the food back to the kitchen and say, "I don't believe I have to ask the chef to keep the sand out of my food". Redmond should state their salt might have sand in it. They don't mention that anywhere. I'm getting rid of this in an electrolyte drink so I at least drink the sand and not chew on it.
